The lowest common ancestor of these entities is the Organonitrogen Compound class, suggesting a shared biochemical pathway. The scores from the paths indicate a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, though the exact nature of the interaction remains unclear. The mechanism appears to involve a chain of events where Tacrolimus indirectly affects Cyp3a7 through the modulation of Factor Ii Deficiency, which is linked to the binding of specific compounds to the enzyme. This suggests a possible role in drug metabolism, though further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct interaction between Tacrolimus and Cyp3a7.
